knowledge-base.name: lang-python
knowledge-base.triggers: Python, .py, pyproject.toml, requirements.txt, pytest, ruff, mypy, uv, poetry, FastAPI, Django, Flask, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy, asyncio, venv
knowledge-base.overview: Language-specific idioms, guardrails, and patterns for Python. Loaded automatically when agents work on .py files or pyproject.toml. Applies to Python 3.11+, APIs, CLIs, data pipelines, and automation.

core-principles.principle: All function signatures, class attributes, and module-level variables must have type annotations.
No `*` imports, no mutable default arguments, no implicit type coercions.
Never install into system Python. Use `venv`, `uv`, or `poetry` for every project.
Use pytest for all testing. Fixtures and `parametrize` over `setUp`/`tearDown`.
Enforce style mechanically. Never rely on manual formatting.

guardrail.rule: Never use bare `except:` or `except Exception:` without re-raising. Always catch specific exceptions.
guardrail.bad: try: result = risky_operation() except: # catches KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit, etc. pass # silently swallows all errors

guardrail.rule: Never use mutable default arguments. They are shared across all calls and cause subtle bugs.
Never use star imports (`from module import *`). They pollute the namespace and break static analysis.
guardrail.bad: from os.path import * from mymodule import *
guardrail.good: from os.path import join, exists, dirname from mymodule import UserService, UserRepository

guardrail.rule: All public functions must have full type annotations: parameters AND return type.
guardrail.good:
from collections.abc import Sequence
def find_users( ids: Sequence[str], *, active_only: bool = True, ) -> list[User]: """Fetch users by ID list, optionally filtering inactive.""" ...

guardrail.rule: Use `raise ... from err` to preserve exception chains. Never log-and-raise — log at the boundary or raise in the interior, not both.
Use `collections.abc` types for annotations (`Sequence`, `Mapping`, `Iterable`), not `list`, `dict` as generics in older code, and never `List`, `Dict` from `typing`.
guardrail.bad: from typing import List, Dict, Optional # deprecated in 3.9+ def process(items: List[str]) -> Optional[Dict[str, int]]: ...
guardrail.good:
from collections.abc import Sequence, Mapping
def process(items: Sequence[str]) -> Mapping[str, int] | None: ...

guardrail.rule: Use `pathlib.Path` instead of `os.path` for all file operations.
guardrail.bad: import os path = os.path.join(base_dir, "data", "users.csv") if os.path.exists(path): with open(path) as f: ...
guardrail.good: from pathlib import Path path = Path(base_dir) / "data" / "users.csv" if path.exists(): with path.open() as f: ...

guardrail.rule: Always use `with` statements or `contextlib.closing` for resources. Never rely on manual `close()` calls.
guardrail.bad: conn = get_connection() result = conn.execute(query) conn.close() # skipped if exception raised above
guardrail.good: with get_connection() as conn: result = conn.execute(query) # conn.close() guaranteed

guardrail.rule: Run `mypy --strict` in CI. No `type: ignore` without an explanatory comment.
guardrail.good: result = some_untyped_lib() # type: ignore[no-untyped-call] -- third-party lib has no stubs (TODO: open issue)

guardrail.rule: Define all dependencies in `pyproject.toml`. Never hand-edit `requirements.txt` — it is a generated artifact only.
Target Python 3.11+. Set `requires-python = ">=3.11"` in `pyproject.toml`. Use `match` statements, `ExceptionGroup`, `tomllib`.
Prefer f-strings over `.format()` or `%` formatting. Use f-strings for all string interpolation in 3.11+.
guardrail.bad: msg = "User %s not found" % user_id msg = "User {} not found".format(user_id)

guardrail.rule: Use `contextlib.suppress()` instead of empty except blocks when intentionally ignoring a specific exception.

directory.purpose: Root for all importable packages (src layout prevents accidental local imports)
PEP 561 marker — tells downstream tools this package ships type stubs
Business logic and entities — no I/O dependencies
Data access layer — database queries, ORM models
Shared fixtures for the entire test suite
Single source of truth for project config, dependencies, and tool settings

project-structure.note: No `__init__.py` in `tests/` — pytest discovers without it. Split modules at ~200 lines.

pattern.name: Exception Hierarchy
pattern.context: All projects — define in domain/exceptions.py before writing services
pattern.description: Typed exception hierarchy with machine-readable error codes. All application exceptions root in a single base class for easy catch-all at boundaries.

pattern.name: Context Manager for Resource Cleanup
pattern.context: Database connections, file handles, network sessions
pattern.description: Use `contextmanager` to guarantee cleanup even on exception. Translate low-level errors to domain errors at the boundary.

pattern.name: Protocol for Structural Subtyping
pattern.context: Abstracting interfaces without inheritance — duck typing with type safety
pattern.description: Use `Protocol` instead of ABCs when you want duck typing with static checking. Clients depend on the structural interface, not a concrete base class.

pattern.name: Dataclass for Value Objects
pattern.context: Data containers without behavior — request/response shapes, domain value objects
pattern.description: Prefer dataclasses or Pydantic over plain dicts for structured data. `frozen=True` enforces immutability.

testing.pattern:
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, patch
async def test_send_notification_retries_on_failure() -> None: mock_client = AsyncMock() mock_client.post.side_effect = [ConnectionError, None]
with patch("myproject.service.notify.http_client", mock_client): await send_notification(user_id="u-123", message="hello")
assert mock_client.post.call_count == 2

rules.rule: Test files: `test_*.py`, same name as module (`models.py` -> `test_models.py`)
Use `conftest.py` for fixtures shared across a directory; nest conftest files for scope
Mark slow tests: `@pytest.mark.slow` and exclude from default runs with `-m "not slow"`
No `unittest.TestCase` — use plain functions with pytest assertions
Use `tmp_path` fixture for file operations (auto-cleanup by pytest)

pyproject-config.description: Canonical pyproject.toml configuration for Python 3.11+ projects.
pyproject-config.example:
[project] name = "myproject" requires-python = ">=3.11"
[project.optional-dependencies] dev = ["ruff", "mypy", "pytest", "pytest-cov", "pytest-asyncio"]
[tool.ruff] target-version = "py311" line-length = 88
[tool.ruff.lint] select = [ "E", # pycodestyle errors "W", # pycodestyle warnings "F", # pyflakes "I", # isort "N", # pep8-naming "UP", # pyupgrade "B", # flake8-bugbear "S", # flake8-bandit (security) "A", # flake8-builtins "C4", # flake8-comprehensions "SIM", # flake8-simplify "RUF", # ruff-specific rules ]
[tool.mypy] strict = true warn_return_any = true disallow_untyped_defs = true
[tool.pytest.ini_options] testpaths = ["tests"] markers = ["slow: marks tests as slow (deselect with '-m \"not slow\"')"] asyncio_mode = "auto"
[tool.coverage.run] source = ["src/myproject"] branch = true
[tool.coverage.report] fail_under = 60 show_missing = true exclude_lines = ["if TYPE_CHECKING:", "pragma: no cover"]

quick-reference.item: All public functions need full annotations — params + return. Run `mypy --strict`.
Use `X | None` not `Optional[X]`; use `X | Y` not `Union[X, Y]`
Never — always name what you import
Never `def f(items=[])` — use `None` and initialize inside the function
Never — log at boundaries, raise in the interior
Use `contextlib.suppress(ExcType)` instead of empty except blocks
Always use `with` — never rely on manual `.close()`
pyproject.toml is the source of truth; requirements.txt is generated only
ruff check + ruff format before every commit
80% business logic minimum, 60% overall; `fail_under = 60` enforced in CI
Use `src/myproject/` to prevent accidental local imports
Include `py.typed` marker for downstream type checking (PEP 561)
